turns.caller: We just bought a house and the previous owner had a system installed by you. Does the warranty transfer?
turns.agent: Partly. The manufacturer parts warranty may transfer once to you as the new homeowner, usually within 90 days of the home sale, and the manufacturer charges a transfer fee of $50–$100. Meridian can provide the transfer form. Meridian's own labor warranty doesn't transfer to a new homeowner.

sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#warranty-tra:
[Warranty Policy — Warranty transfer (effective 2025-06-15)]
- Manufacturer parts warranties may transfer once to a subsequent homeowner, usually within 90 days of the home sale and subject to a manufacturer transfer fee ($50–$100). Meridian can provide the transfer form.
- Meridian labor warranties do **not** transfer to a new homeowner.
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#tran:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Transfer (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Memberships are tied to the service address and transfer to a new homeowner at the same address. They do not transfer to a new address.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#new-system-i:
[Warranty Policy — New system installation warranty (effective 2025-06-15)]
- Meridian provides a **2-year labor warranty** on all full system installations.
- Comfort Club members at the time of installation receive an extended **5-year labor warranty**.
- Manufacturer parts warranties are separate and vary by brand (see table below). Meridian registers every installed unit with the manufacturer within 30 days of install. Registration is required for the full parts warranty term; unregistered units typically receive only 5 years.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#filing-a-cla:
[Warranty Policy — Filing a claim (effective 2025-06-15)]
Call to schedule a warranty diagnostic. If the failure is covered, there is no diagnostic fee. If the technician determines the failure is not covered, the standard $89 diagnostic fee applies.

sections.services/technician_arrival_and_etas.md#:
[Technician Arrival Windows and Delays]
Appointment windows are 4-hour blocks. Technicians arrive at any point within the window.
If a technician is running late:
1. Dispatch will text the customer with an updated ETA.
2. If the technician will miss the window entirely, the customer can reschedule at no charge.
Customers are not required to wait past the window. A missed window is never charged as a no-show.

- Standard appointment windows are 8am–12pm, 12pm–4pm, and 1pm–5pm. A 4pm–7pm window is available Tuesday and Thursday only.

- Cancellations or reschedules more than 24 hours before the window are free. Inside 24 hours there is a $49 late-cancellation fee. No-shows (nobody home at the address) are charged the full diagnostic fee.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

turns.caller: I need to schedule a service call. My thermostat is blank.
turns.agent: Happy to help with that. First I need to verify your account. Could you give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?

turns.caller: Derek Brown. My account number is MHC-53209.
turns.agent:
Thanks, Derek, you're verified. Before we book, here are a few quick checks for a blank thermostat:

1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan. A full drain pan can cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there's standing water, a drain line clearing would be the right visit.

Want to try those, or should I go ahead and find appointment times?

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

turns.caller: Does the labor warranty cover a repeat repair? You fixed my blower in March and it's doing the same thing.

sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#repair-warra:
[Warranty Policy — Repair warranty (Meridian labor warranty) (effective 2025-06-15)]
- All repairs performed by Meridian carry a **1-year labor warranty** on the specific part repaired or replaced.
- If the same part fails within 1 year, the return visit and labor are free. Parts are covered if they were supplied by Meridian.
- The repair warranty does not cover different components, pre-existing conditions noted on the original invoice, or failures caused by lack of maintenance, power surges, or customer modifications.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#new-system-i:
[Warranty Policy — New system installation warranty (effective 2025-06-15)]
- Meridian provides a **2-year labor warranty** on all full system installations.
- Comfort Club members at the time of installation receive an extended **5-year labor warranty**.
- Manufacturer parts warranties are separate and vary by brand (see table below). Meridian registers every installed unit with the manufacturer within 30 days of install. Registration is required for the full parts warranty term; unregistered units typically receive only 5 years.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#manufacturer:

| Rheem | 10 years | 10 years | 20 years |
| American Standard | 10 years | 10 years | 20 years |
Note: Manufacturer warranties cover the **part only**. Labor to replace a warranted part is billable after the Meridian labor warranty expires.

- Manufacturer parts warranties may transfer once to a subsequent homeowner, usually within 90 days of the home sale and subject to a manufacturer transfer fee ($50–$100). Meridian can provide the transfer form.
- Meridian labor warranties do **not** transfer to a new homeowner.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Scheduling (effective 2026-03-02)]
- Standard appointment windows are 8am–12pm, 12pm–4pm, and 1pm–5pm. A 4pm–7pm window is available Tuesday and Thursday only.
- You will receive a text the morning of your appointment with the technician's name and photo, and another text when the tech is 30 minutes away.
- Cancellations or reschedules more than 24 hours before the window are free. Inside 24 hours there is a $49 late-cancellation fee. No-shows (nobody home at the address) are charged the full diagnostic fee.
sections.services/technician_arrival_and_etas.md#:
[Technician Arrival Windows and Delays]
Appointment windows are 4-hour blocks. Technicians arrive at any point within the window.
If a technician is running late:
1. Dispatch will text the customer with an updated ETA.
2. If the technician will miss the window entirely, the customer can reschedule at no charge.
Customers are not required to wait past the window. A missed window is never charged as a no-show.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#f:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Furnace won't turn on]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop immediately and follow the safety protocol.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.

turns.caller: What does the Comfort Club membership actually include?
turns.agent: The standard Comfort Club ($189/year per system, or $16.99/month) includes two seasonal tune-ups a year (one cooling, one heating), priority scheduling, and a waived $89 diagnostic fee. It also includes 15% off all repairs, no after-hours dispatch fee on emergency calls, and annual reminder and filter-change notifications. Comfort Club Plus ($269/year) adds an annual water heater flush and inspection, an annual whole-home plumbing inspection, and 15% off plumbing repairs. Both tiers get $500 off a full system replacement.

sections.services/technician_arrival_and_etas.md#:
[Technician Arrival Windows and Delays]
Appointment windows are 4-hour blocks. Technicians arrive at any point within the window.
If a technician is running late:
1. Dispatch will text the customer with an updated ETA.
2. If the technician will miss the window entirely, the customer can reschedule at no charge.
Customers are not required to wait past the window. A missed window is never charged as a no-show.
sections.faq/customer_faq.md#scheduling-0:

- Standard appointment windows are 8am–12pm, 12pm–4pm, and 1pm–5pm. A 4pm–7pm window is available Tuesday and Thursday only.
- You will receive a text the morning of your appointment with the technician's name and photo, and another text when the tech is 30 minutes away.
- Cancellations or reschedules more than 24 hours before the window are free. Inside 24 hours there is a $49 late-cancellation fee. No-shows (nobody home at the address) are charged the full diagnostic fee.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

turns.caller: I need to schedule a service call. The furnace won't kick on.
turns.agent: Happy to help with that. First I need to verify your account. Could you give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?

turns.agent:
Thanks, Jennifer, you're verified. Before I book, here are a few quick checks that sometimes fix it:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above the room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (it looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.
5. If you smell gas at any point, stop right away and follow the gas safety protocol.

Want to try these, or should I go ahead and find appointment times?

sections.faq/customer_faq.md#payment-0:
[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Payment (effective 2026-03-02)]
- We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, and ACH.
- We do not accept checks or cash from technicians in the field.
- Card numbers are never taken over the phone. Agents send a secure payment link by text or email, valid for 24 hours.
- Financing is available on repairs over $1,000 and all system replacements through our financing partner. Approval takes about 5 minutes.
sections.membership/comfort_club_overview.md#bill:
[Comfort Club Maintenance Plan — Billing and renewal (effective 2026-01-01)]
- Annual plans bill once on the enrollment date and auto-renew each year on the same date.
- Monthly plans bill on the enrollment day of each month and require a 12-month minimum commitment.
- Members receive a renewal reminder email 30 days before renewal.
- Existing members are locked at their enrollment price until their next renewal date, at which point the current price applies.
sections.warranty/warranty_policy.md#repair-warra:
[Warranty Policy — Repair warranty (Meridian labor warranty) (effective 2025-06-15)]
- All repairs performed by Meridian carry a **1-year labor warranty** on the specific part repaired or replaced.
- If the same part fails within 1 year, the return visit and labor are free. Parts are covered if they were supplied by Meridian.
- The repair warranty does not cover different components, pre-existing conditions noted on the original invoice, or failures caused by lack of maintenance, power surges, or customer modifications.
sections.faq/customer_faq.md#duplicate-charges-0:
[Meridian Home Comfort — Customer FAQ — Duplicate charges (effective 2026-03-02)]
If you see two charges, one is usually a pending authorization that drops off in 3–5 business days. If both post, contact us and we will open a case with our payment processor.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

turns.caller: The AC. It's not cooling at all. The fan runs but the air coming out is warm.
turns.agent:
Before I book, here are a few quick checks you can try:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to COOL and below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter and replace it if it's dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop.
4. Look at the outdoor unit for debris, or a fan that isn't spinning.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw.

Have you already tried these, or would you like me to book the warranty diagnostic visit now?

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

turns.caller: My Carrier compressor died and the system is only three years old. Is that under warranty?
turns.agent: Most likely yes for the part. Carrier compressors carry a 10-year manufacturer warranty when the unit is registered, and unregistered units typically get 5 years, so your system should be within either term. That covers the part only. Labor is billable once Meridian's labor warranty ends, which is 2 years on a full installation (5 years if you were a Comfort Club member at install). A warranty diagnostic is free if the failure is covered, but if the technician finds it isn't covered, the standard $89 diagnostic fee applies.

turns.caller: It's the AC. It's not cooling at all. The fan runs but the air is warm.
turns.agent:
Before we book, here are a few quick checks you can try.

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter and replace it if it's dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Look at the outdoor unit. If it's covered in debris or its fan isn't spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF with the fan ON for 2 hours to thaw it.

If you've already tried these or would rather skip them, I'll find you a warranty diagnostic time.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

transcript: caller: Hey, so the furnace won't kick on. What's the soonest you can get a tech out?

agent: Sorry your furnace isn't kicking on. I can help get a tech out. First, I need to verify your account. Could you give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?
caller: Sure. James Patel, account number MHC-13766.

agent: Thanks, James, you're verified. Before I book, here are a few quick checks that sometimes get a furnace running:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (it looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.

If you smell gas at any point, stop and follow the safety protocol. If you've already tried these or would rather skip them, tell me and I'll find the soonest openings.

caller: Thanks. I already checked the thermostat and the breaker, and they look fine. I haven't looked at the switch or the filter yet, but I'd rather just get a tech out. No gas smell. Can you find me a slot this Saturday afternoon?

agent: I don't have any Saturday afternoon openings. These are the soonest options:

1. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Ray Mendoza
2. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski
3. Mon Oct 19, 8am–12pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski

Would you like one of these?
caller: Monday is fine if Saturday isn't open. I'll take option 1, Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm with Ray Mendoza. Before you book it, is the $89 diagnostic fee on this visit? I'm okay with it if so.
agent: Just to confirm: book Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit, technician Ray Mendoza?
caller: Yes, please book that one. Mon Oct 19, 12pm to 4pm with Ray Mendoza. And yes, I understand the $89 diagnostic fee applies. I agree.

agent: You're booked for Monday, Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, for a furnace repair visit with Ray Mendoza.

The $89 diagnostic fee applies to this visit. It's credited toward the repair if you approve the repair during the same visit. If the technician confirms the failure is covered by warranty, there's no diagnostic fee.
caller: Thanks, that works. Just to confirm, the unit is a Trane. I agree to the $89 diagnostic fee.
agent: Thanks, James. I've noted that it's a Trane furnace, and you can also tell Ray when he arrives. Your visit is set for Monday, Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, and the $89 diagnostic fee is understood.
caller: Sounds good, thanks. That's all I needed. [DONE]

judge.why: The assistant booked the Mon Oct 19 12pm–4pm visit with Ray Mendoza after saying Saturday afternoon wasn't available. Its $89 diagnostic fee, credit and warranty statements match the KB. It then said "I've noted that it's a Trane furnace." Nothing it retrieved or did shows a note was saved, so that claim is unsupported. The caller's goal was still met.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#t:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Thermostat screen is blank]
1. Replace the batteries if it has them.
2. Check the breaker for the air handler.
3. Check the float switch in the condensate pan — a full drain pan will cut power to the thermostat on many systems. If there is standing water, book a drain line clearing.

transcript: caller: Hi, I'm calling to book a repair. There's water pooling around the indoor unit.

agent: Sorry to hear that. I can help you book a repair. First, I need to verify your account. Can I get your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?
caller: Sure. My name is Daniel Baker. My account number is MHC-48506.

agent: Thanks, Daniel, you're verified. Water pooling at the indoor unit is usually a clogged condensate drain line. Please turn the system off to prevent overflow damage, and don't pour bleach into the line unless a technician tells you to. Have you already turned it off? If so, I'll look up repair times for you.
caller: Yes, I turned it off. Can you check for a Saturday afternoon slot? If you have anything earlier than that, I'd take it.

agent: I don't have a Saturday afternoon opening, and nothing earlier than these. The soonest are on Monday, October 19:

2. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski
3. Mon Oct 19, 8am–12pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski

Would you like one of these? There's no cancellation waitlist, but you're welcome to check back for earlier openings.
caller: The earliest one is best for me, so I'll take option 3, Monday Oct 19, 8am to 12pm with Marta Kowalski.

agent: The options were renumbered when I rechecked, so I need to confirm with you again. These are the current options:

1. Mon Oct 19, 8am–12pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski
2. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Ray Mendoza
3. Mon Oct 19, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Marta Kowalski

Should I book option 1, Monday Oct 19, 8am–12pm with Marta Kowalski?
caller: Yes, option 1 works. Monday Oct 19, 8am to 12pm with Marta Kowalski. Please book it.
agent: You're booked, Daniel. Marta Kowalski will come for your repair visit on Monday, October 19, between 8am and 12pm. Please keep the system off until she arrives.
caller: Thanks. Before I go, is there a diagnostic fee for this visit? I'm fine with it if there is.
agent: Yes, there's an $89 diagnostic fee. It's credited toward the repair if you approve the repair during the same visit. It's waived for Comfort Club members.

caller: I agree.

Also, the unit's brand is probably Lennox, since it came with the house. Thanks, that's all I needed.

turns.agent: I'm sorry your furnace isn't kicking on. I can help get someone out. First I need to verify your account. Could you give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?

turns.caller: Raj Okafor. My account number is MHC-78738.
turns.agent:
Thanks, Raj, you're verified. Before I book, here are a few quick checks that sometimes fix this:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above the room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (it looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.

If you smell gas at any point, stop right away and follow the gas safety protocol. If you've already tried these or would rather skip them, tell me and I'll find appointment times.

sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#a:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — AC not cooling or blowing warm air]
1. Confirm the thermostat is set to COOL and the set point is below room temperature.
2. Check the air filter. A clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow. Replace if dirty.
3. Check the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker once. If it trips again, stop and book a visit.
4. Check the outdoor unit. If it is covered in debris or the fan is not spinning, book a visit.
5. If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF (fan ON) for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
sections.faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md#w:
[Before You Call: Quick Checks — Water pooling at the indoor unit]
This is almost always a clogged condensate drain line. Turn the system off to prevent overflow damage and book a visit. Do not pour bleach into the line unless instructed by a technician.

Booked: Wed Oct 21, 8am–12pm, repair visit, technician Jun Park.

transcript: caller: Hi, the furnace won't kick on and I'd like to get someone out to look at it.

agent: I'm sorry your furnace isn't kicking on. I can help get someone out. First I need to verify your account. Could you give me your full name and one of these: your account number, the phone number on the account, or your service address?
caller: Raj Okafor. My account number is MHC-78738.

agent: Thanks, Raj, you're verified. Before I book, here are a few quick checks that sometimes fix this:

1. Make sure the thermostat is set to HEAT and the set point is above the room temperature.
2. Check that the furnace switch (it looks like a light switch near the unit) is ON.
3. Check the breaker.
4. Check the filter.

If you smell gas at any point, stop right away and follow the gas safety protocol. If you've already tried these or would rather skip them, tell me and I'll find appointment times.
caller: I haven't tried those yet. I'll check the thermostat and the switch now. I don't know where the breaker is, so I'll skip that one. Should I just book the visit anyway if those don't fix it?

agent: Yes, if the thermostat and switch don't fix it, just tell me and I'll find you appointment times. The filter is also worth a quick look if you can reach it. Our diagnostic visit is $89, and it's credited toward the repair if you go ahead with one.

caller: Okay, thanks. I checked the thermostat and it's set to heat, but the furnace still won't kick on. The switch is on too. I'm not sure about the filter, so let's just book the visit. Can you find me a Thursday morning slot, 8 to noon?

agent: I don't have a Thursday morning opening. These are the closest options:

1. Wed Oct 21, 8am–12pm, repair visit with Jun Park
2. Wed Oct 21, 1pm–5pm, repair visit with Jun Park
3. Fri Oct 23, 12pm–4pm, repair visit with Jun Park

Would you like one of these? I can also look for something earlier.
caller: Hmm, Wednesday morning 8 to 12 is the closest to what I wanted. I'll take option 1.
agent: Just to confirm: book Wed Oct 21, 8am–12pm, repair visit, technician Jun Park?
caller: Yes, please book that one.

agent: You're booked, Raj. Jun Park will be there Wednesday, Oct 21, between 8am and noon for a furnace repair visit. If there's anything the technician should know, like where the unit is or how to get in, you can tell them when they arrive.

caller: Thanks, that works. Jun will need to get into the house, so I'll leave the door open for them. Thanks for the help.

[DONE]

It booked the Wed Oct 21 8am–12pm visit the caller chose, after saying no Thursday morning slot was open. The $89 diagnostic fee, credited toward a repair, matches the KB. Nothing stated contradicts the sources.
